run_by: newsroom.writer, at the editor's request, as a fresh look after the corrections of v0.13.104
summary: The article's numbers reproduce from the primary sources: the CVE record's timestamp, NVD's 1,394 for the window and its daily and status breakdown, the absence of Exploit-DB or Metasploit references, the 25 VulnCheck CVEs with old-year IDs, CISA's catalogue dates and version, the EPSS bands and daily series, all four yearly totals, and the PHP story site's 53 compromise rows and Pulse counts; all nine of ChatGPT's fixes hold in the current text, and every quote of Jeremiah Grossman's post matches the screenshot. Fix first: the VulnCheck row says 'the count matches' when the post counts 24 old bugs and the article's NVD query finds 25, so the two counts are near but not the same; after that, the five links to the PHP data site's version 0.1.77 files now return 404.

facts.notes: Re-ran NVD's CVE API 2.0 for the window (1,394, with the status, day, ID-year and assigner breakdowns), FIRST's EPSS for all 1,394 at the 26 October scores and the three-CVE time series, CISA's KEV JSON (version 2026.10.26, 1,758 entries, additions per year to 26 October), the four CVE records at cveawg.mitre.org, and NVD's yearly totals in chunks of at most 120 days for 2023 to 2026. Read Fortinet's and Wiz's posts, the PHP story site's compromise, exploitation, claims, numbers and pulse files at version 0.1.77 through its manifest and blob store, the KEV-listing-run report, the brief for the PHP team, and the linked bounty article. Compared every quote of the post against the screenshot. One count presented as matching does not (f1); the heading's 1,393 is off by one (f3); one NVD status count has moved (f4).

voice.notes: First person, the post's claims and the article's own verdicts kept apart, limits stated. No em dashes, superlatives or hype found; the only 'nobody has' is inside a quotation of the post. One punctuation slip (f6).

claims.notes: What was read, what was not (VulnCheck's KEV, Censys's dashboard) and what is forecast rather than observed are marked, in the table, the body and the limits. The watchTowr honeypot claim is correctly left unconfirmed: the PHP site's claims file marks it 'unverified: watchtowr.com returns HTTP 403'.

conversions.notes: Recomputed: 274/210 = 1.305 (30%); 89,531/40,266 = 2.22 (more than twice); the shares 0.616%, 0.454%, 0.522%, 0.306% round to the stated 0.62%, 0.45%, 0.52%, 0.31%. The same-number check was done across the summary, In short, the table, the captions and the body; one rounding differs between the summary and the body (f5).

health.notes: All newsroom, PHP story site, team site and vendor links answered 200 on 27 October, except the five data links at version 0.1.77, which answered 404 (f2). The graph's six quotes appear in the page text. The seven figure files exist and the captions match the body. The compromise line is unchanged at the latest data version (0.1.82, as of 12:13 UTC on 27 October, now 56 rows). No folded section summaries were found in the page, so none were checked.

people.notes: Jeremiah Grossman is a public author of a public post, named with his title as the screenshot shows it. The eight organisations are named from published statements captured by the PHP story site. No key or token in the text or the dataset.

findings.quote: The count matches; KEV membership and when the IDs were assigned not checked
findings.issue: The post says 25 CVEs are on VulnCheck's KEV and that 24 of those 25 are old bugs given IDs on 22 October. The article's NVD query finds 25 VulnCheck-assigned CVEs with 2017 to 2025 IDs, all published on 22 October, and calls that a matching count. It matches the post's 25 only if the old-bug count is 25, but the post puts it at 24, with one further entry that is not an old bug. The two counts are near, not the same, and the summary's 'VulnCheck published 25 old bugs' and the window section's 'matches the count and the pattern' carry the same mismatch.
findings.evidence: The screenshot of the post, admin/content/articles/images/jg-post.webp, and https://services.nvd.nist.gov/rest/json/cves/2.0?pubStartDate=2026-10-21T13:48:34.000&pubEndDate=2026-10-25T13:48:34.000&resultsPerPage=2000, read 27 October 2026 at 15:44 UTC
findings.source_passage: VulnCheck puts 25 of the 1,448 (1.7%) on its KEV list, its catalog of bugs adversaries have been seen exploiting. 24 of those 25 are old bugs. VulnCheck only now gave them CVE IDs, all at once on October 22, with ID years from 2017 to 2025.
findings.method: From the NVD window response, filter sourceIdentifier == disclosure@vulncheck.com and ID year != 2026: 25 records, all with published date 2026-10-22, ID years 2017 to 2025 (CVE-2017-20287 to CVE-2025-71434). The post's figure for old bugs is 24; 25 is its total on VulnCheck's KEV including one entry that is not an old bug.
findings.suggestion: Say 'NVD shows 25 old-ID VulnCheck CVEs against the post's 24 of 25: close, not the same' in the table, the summary and the window section, and keep the KEV-membership caveat.

findings.quote: The PHP story site's data at version 0.1.77
findings.issue: The five links to compromise.json, exploitation.json, claims.json, numbers.json and pulse.json at /v/0.1.77/ return 404. The data site serves only its newest five versions at plain paths, and the latest is now 0.1.82, so the pinned version the article's counts come from has dropped off the plain path. The content is still reachable: /v/0.1.77/manifest.json still answers, and each file's sha256 there resolves at /blobs/<sha256>.
findings.evidence: https://data.php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/v/0.1.77/compromise.json (404), https://data.php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/v/0.1.77/manifest.json (200), https://data.php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/ and versions.json (latest 0.1.82), read 27 October 2026 at 15:44 UTC
findings.source_passage: The newest 5 versions are also served plain, at /v/<version>/<file>. Latest: v0.1.82
findings.method: curl each of the five article URLs: all return HTTP 404 with the GitHub Pages not-found page. curl /v/0.1.77/manifest.json: 200; the sha256 for compromise.json there is 7582d4c6168e59f1ad58d609737538bb0c0709b4c27461f2c4adc73ecf708352 and /blobs/ of that hash returns the 26,534-byte file with as_of 2026-10-27T09:43Z and 53 rows.
findings.suggestion: Link the five files by their blob hashes, or link the version's manifest.json and say the plain paths expire after five versions.
